note: MAPPING paper_explicit. S1 Appendix 'CQ and Sustainable Innovation Behavior Questionnaire' (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0250878.s001, DOCX, read with python-docx) heads its fourth block 'Sustainable innovation behavior' and numbers exactly six items 1-6; the S2 response workbook's header carries SIB1..SIB6, and S2 File's own descriptive table (.s003) labels that same row block 'sustainable innovation behavior', so the block header plus the 1-6 numbering ties each sentence to a column. CODE DERIVATION is core-model pattern 1, nothing to get wrong: data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py (one script emits all four sibling tables) selects [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('SIB')] and melts with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- no rename and no positional step. LEVEL-1 CHECKED AND ABSENT: .s002 is a bare WPS .xls, one sheet, 41 header cells (ID + 9 covariates + SIB1-6 + CQ1-12 + KS1-4 + OCD1-9), with no variable or value labels at either level, so the appendix is the highest available source. VERIFICATION (verify_li_2021_sustainable_innov_behav.R, PARTIAL): route 1 -- refitting the paper's own one-factor CFA of the SIB construct on the four items its Table 2 retained reproduces the published standardized loadings to 0.0004 and the R-SQUARE column to 0.0003 (SIB1 0.707/0.500, SIB2 0.903/0.815, SIB3 0.775/0.601, SIB6 0.754/0.569 published vs 0.7072/0.5002, 0.9026/0.8147, 0.7752/0.6010, 0.7544/0.5691 observed on n=336); Table 2 is an image and these numbers exist in no machine-readable form. A sweep of all 360 ordered 4-of-6 assignments puts the shipped one uniquely first at SSD 0.000000 against 0.000878 for the runner-up. Route 8 -- the article says two SIB items were dropped because their 'residual error values ... were not independent and were strongly correlated', and the pair absent from Table 2 is {SIB4,SIB5}; the sentences shipped for SIB4 and SIB5 are the block's only implementation pair, and SIB4-SIB5 is empirically the tightest pair in the data on both measures (raw r = 0.738, the largest of the 15; one-factor residual correlation 0.120 against 0.073 for the next largest). PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: nothing in the data orders the two implementation sentences against each other (SIB4 vs SIB5) or separates the SIB1 vs SIB3 sentences, so those rest on the appendix numbering alone. STEP 3b, clean: 6 items on 1-7 with n=336 each matches the paper's 336 valid questionnaires and the appendix's six-item SIB block, and both sample items the Measures section quotes for this scale ('I often come up with creative ideas', and a paraphrase of appendix item 4) are in the shipped text -- the live content is sustainable innovation behaviour, not the siblings' CQ1-12, KS1-4 or OCD1-9. DEVIATIONS: leading item numbering ('1.'..'6.') stripped, each stripped number asserted equal to the code's numeric suffix first; appendix item 2 is typed '2.：I often come up with creative ideas.' and the stray full-width colon left by the numbering was stripped with it -- nothing else in any sentence was altered. instructions holds the appendix cover paragraph verbatim, its Word line breaks joined into one paragraph (whole-questionnaire framing shared with the three sibling tables; the SIB block carries no instruction line of its own), so section_prompt is blank and there is a single trivial section_id. option_text is blank at all seven levels: the appendix prints each item's scale as seven unlabelled boxes ('1□ 2□ 3□ 4 □5 □6 □7 □') and the paper says only 'a Likert 7-point scale', so no anchors exist in any source and no point was padded with its own number. correct_response empty (attitude scale, no key). LANGUAGE: administered in Chinese -- INFERRED, not stated. The paper never names an administration language nor says the appendix is a translation, but the sample is 336 valid responses from employees of 31 Chinese enterprises, the authors are at a Chinese university, and .s002's OLE metadata reads Locale ID 2052 (zh-CN), creating application WPS. No Chinese wording exists anywhere in the deposit or the paper's own supplements (S1 Appendix body is entirely English; .s002 holds only integers and English headers; .s003 is a statistics table), so the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: the authors' own English ships in the base fields, the four _translated columns are emitted empty, language=Chinese is retained as the backfill signal, and translation_source=study_supplied because nothing was translated by this project. RIGHTS: no restriction to quote. The article and all three supplements are CC BY 4.0 and the wording was copied from the CC BY supplement; the source scale (Scott & Bruce 1994, Academy of Management Journal 37(3):580-607, modified by these authors) carries no fee and no redistribution bar that could be found or quoted, so under the 2026-09-04 quote test silence is permission. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, table shipped.

note: Source: Li Y, Fan Y, Lin J, Shi S (2024) PeerJ 12:e17910, doi:10.7717/peerj.17910 (CC BY 4.0); deposit peerj-12-17910-s001.xlsx via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint for PMC11332389. INSTRUMENT MISMATCH (Step 3b): the IRW dictionary Description calls this a '4-item body-image scale subset', which is wrong. BDYZ is the paper's Expressive Suppression Scale (pinyin biaoda yizhi), the four-item expressive-suppression subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (Gross & John 2003; Chinese version per Zhao et al. 2015), scored 1-7 'Strongly Disagree' to 'Strongly Agree'. The body-image measure in this study is the separate 15-item SPA block (li_2024_spa). Confirmed against the data, not just the name: summing BDYZ1/2/6/9 raw reproduces the paper's published Expressive Suppression total exactly (mean 14.66, SD 5.61, N=1,151 vs published 14.66/5.61/1,151), Cronbach's alpha is 0.8336 vs the published 0.834, and the correlation with the correctly reverse-scored SPA total is 0.219, the exact value in the paper's Table 2. CODE DERIVATION: number-preserving rename -- data/li_2024_socialavoidance.py melts BDYZ1/BDYZ2/BDYZ6/BDYZ9 and rewrites the code as 'bdyz_' + the trailing digits, so bdyz_N is column BDYZN. No positional assignment. MAPPING: the .xlsx carries bare column names and no variable or value labels, so no level-1 source exists in the deposit and the wording had to come from the instrument. The ERQ numbers its suppression items 2, 4, 6, 9; the deposit ships 1, 2, 6, 9. bdyz_2/bdyz_6/bdyz_9 take ERQ items 2/6/9 by the instrument's own numbering, corroborated by the paper's one explicit code-to-content tie ('item 9, "I don't express sadness and anger when I feel it"', which is ERQ item 9, the negative-emotion suppression item). bdyz_1 is assigned ERQ item 4 BY ELIMINATION: it is unambiguously a suppression item (corrected item-total r = 0.628, in line with 0.652/0.695/0.678 for the other three, and the four-item alpha reproduces the published value), so it cannot be ERQ item 1, which is a cognitive-reappraisal item; ERQ item 4 is the only suppression item otherwise unaccounted for. Weak corroboration only: bdyz_1 has the lowest item-total of the four, as the positive-emotion item 4 typically does. This is an inference and is flagged in the public_note. DIRECTION: no reverse scoring, and that is verified rather than assumed -- the raw sum reproduces the published mean of 14.66 (a reversed reading would give 17.34 on this symmetric 1-7 scale). ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: Chinese (Chinese college students, Questionstar online survey). No Chinese wording exists anywhere in the deposit or the paper's supplements -- the .xlsx has ASCII headers only, and s002.docx/s003.docx contain zero CJK characters and only describe scoring and licensing. The fallback therefore applies: the ERQ's own English sits in the base fields, the _translated columns are empty, and language=Chinese. OPTION TEXT: only the two extreme anchors are published ('Strongly Disagree' / 'Strongly Agree', capitalised as in supplement s002); scale points 2-6 are unlabelled in the source and are left blank, not padded. RIGHTS: no quotable restriction from the ERQ's rights holder -- Gross's lab distributes the ERQ free with no fee and no redistribution clause; the paper states the authors licensed it for use in Chinese populations. Silence is permission.
public_note: Item text is the ERQ's original English; this study administered the scale in Chinese and no Chinese wording is published in the deposit or its supplements. The deposit also numbers the four expressive-suppression columns 1, 2, 6, 9 while the ERQ numbers its suppression items 2, 4, 6, 9, so bdyz_1 carries ERQ item 4 ("When I am feeling positive emotions, I am careful not to express them") by elimination rather than by a stated correspondence, and nothing in the data distinguishes item 2 from item 6
